blocks.text: How AI Changes SMM Results

Imagine this: six months ago, two nearly identical coffee shops, A and B, opened in your neighborhood. Same budget, same-quality beans, both launched their social media.

Today, Coffee Shop A has 12K engaged followers and a line out the door every morning. Coffee Shop B has 800 followers and struggles to fill tables.

What's the difference?
Coffee Shop B: AI as a Content Machine

Coffee Shop B uses AI like most people do — as a content generator. Every morning, they open ChatGPT and ask: "Give me 5 Instagram captions for a coffee shop."

They post daily and create Reels because it seems to work for others. Their approach is generate, post, repeat.
Coffee Shop A: AI as a Strategic Partner
Coffee Shop A uses AI in a completely different way. Before creating anything, they use AI to understand, plan, and decide. Content creation is actually the next step in their process.
Before they post anything, they ask ChatGPT:

• "Analyze why someone would choose a specialty coffee shop. What are their real pain points?"
  • "I have three content ideas: a latte art tutorial, a bean sourcing story, or a barista interview. Which aligns best with my goal of attracting morning commuters?"
  • "Should I post this or save it? Does it serve my strategy, or am I just filling my calendar?"

After these strategic questions, Coffee Shop A asks AI to help create content. 

And even then, they're specific: "Write an Instagram caption about our Ethiopian beans that speaks to people who care about sustainable sourcing and want to feel good about their coffee choice. Conversational tone, include a question at the end."

blocks.text: Real Example: How AI Transformed Nike's Social Media Strategy

Everyone knows Nike — a leader in the sports clothing industry. They also lead in leveraging AI for social media advertising, proving that AI isn't just for efficiency — it's a competitive advantage. One of their most notable campaigns was #Nike50, which used AI to explore Serena Williams' career evolution and simulate matches between different versions of the tennis champion across eras. By using AI to analyze data, personalize content, and create dynamic visuals, Nike reached millions of people with content that felt both innovative and emotionally compelling.

The takeaway? Companies that use AI strategically — not just as a content generator, but as a tool for insight, personalization, and creativity — see measurably better results. Whether you're Nike or a local coffee shop, the principle is the same: AI amplifies what works when used thoughtfully. Now, let's see how to implement AI across the entire workflow.
AI Across the Entire SMM Workflow
Think of your social media marketing as a five-stage process:
1. Understand: Who is your audience? What do they care about?
2. Strategize: What should you say? On which platforms?
3. Create: How do you bring this message to life?
4. Optimize: What should you adjust before posting?
5. Analyze: What worked and why?
Strategy First, Content Second

Most of the work happens even before posting anything. First, you need to understand who your audience is, what they care about, and what actually motivates them. This is where AI creates the biggest advantage: helping you make smarter decisions before anything goes live.
Let's see how this plays out in a real-world scenario with AI. For audience understanding, you need signals from real conversations, reviews, and local behavior. We'll use Perplexity for this task.

They value community hubs that offer quality coffee, quick service, and social/work spaces, with motivations centered on convenience, taste, and affordability. Key Motivations and Values — Convenience and Speed: On-the-go customers seek fast mobile ordering and grab-and-go options for busy mornings. — Quality and Experience: Aficionados prioritize specialty brews, ambiance, and barista interactions; health-conscious patrons (e.g., Gen Z) favor low-sugar, plant-based, or organic items. — Social/Workspace Role: Groups and workers want cozy seating, reliable WiFi, outlets, and non-messy snacks for lingering. — Community Ties: Loyalty stems from local vibes, events, and personalization over chains. blocks.text: AI Strategy by Platform

Once you have a clear understanding of your audience, AI helps you adapt your content for different platforms. Each platform plays its own role in how people discover, trust, and engage with your brand.

• Instagram — visual storytelling through photos, Reels, and Stories 
  • Facebook — community building and conversation
  • TikTok — short-form video content with strong discovery potential 
  • LinkedIn — professional networking and B2B connections 
  • Twitter/X — real-time opinions and news sharing
  • YouTube — long-form content and long-term visibility
Repurposing Content
Coffee Shop A doesn't create content from scratch every time. They strategically reuse and repurpose — with AI's help.
Take one blog post: "5 Signs You're Drinking Bad Coffee." AI helps Coffee Shop A transform it into:

• A carousel post with one sign per slide for Instagram
  • A one-minute video on TikTok
  • A discussion post asking followers to share their coffee pet peeves on Facebook
  • A LinkedIn article about quality standards in small food businesses
One core idea, four different formats, each optimized for its platform.

Let's say we want to turn it into a carousel. The initial post looks like this: 5 Signs You’re Drinking Bad Coffee "If your coffee tastes burnt or bitter, feels watery, upsets your stomach, loses flavor too quickly, or you need multiple cups to wake up, it's a warning. Bad beans or poor brewing are usually the cause. Switch to fresh, quality coffee for a better start."

Slide 3 – Sign #2 No roast date on the beans If you don't know when it was roasted, it's probably stale. Slide 4 – Sign #3 You need sugar to enjoy it Great coffee tastes good before add-ons. Slide 5 – Sign #4 It smells burnt or flat Aroma should be rich, not lifeless. Slide 6 – Sign #5 + CTA It's been sitting too long Fresh coffee = better flavor. This repurposing approach works because it multiplies the impact of every strategic decision you make.

Instead of constantly starting from zero, you let AI help you adapt what already works — saving time, reducing burnout, and keeping your message consistent across platforms.

That’s how strong brands stay visible without posting just to stay busy.
This purpose goes beyond content efficiency. When used strategically, social media becomes a core business tool — not just a publishing channel. Used well, it drives measurable business results.
Successful businesses use social media strategically to:

• Communicate directly with customers and respond in real time
  • Market cost-effectively without relying on large ad budgets
  • Build brand awareness through consistent, recognizable messaging
  • Drive sales by promoting offers and products intentionally
  • Understand customers through comments, messages, and feedback

feedbackCorrect.text: Great! Chasing every trend wastes time and dilutes your brand. Smart marketers use AI to evaluate trends: "Does it align with my brand values? Can I participate authentically? Will my audience care?" Analyze first, create second.

feedbackIncorrect.text: This scatter-shot approach might occasionally work, but it's inefficient and unfocused. AI's value lies in helping you filter opportunities and invest your energy where it matters.

blocks.text: Surface-Level Understanding

Effective Content Strategy

In the previous lessons, you've learned how AI helps you analyze audience behavior, uncover real pain points, and identify patterns in what people respond to — not just what they like.

In this lesson, you'll learn how to plan content — choosing what to create, what to skip, and where to focus your limited time for the greatest impact.
What Is a Content Strategy?
A content strategy provides structure for your social media work. It helps you decide what to create — and just as importantly, what to skip — so every post supports a purpose.
It's a clear plan that defines:

• Which content themes support your business goals
  • What topics actually matter to your audience
  • Which types of content drive engagement, trust, or action
With a strategy in place, you stop posting randomly and start creating with intention.

Most profiles miss this opportunity due to vague bios, unclear value propositions, or confusing messaging.

You've defined your content strategy, identified your audience, and optimized your profile to hook visitors. 

But communication doesn't end when someone hits follow. That's where it begins!

When your content reflects your audience's real concerns, followers don't just consume — they respond. That response is what turns followers into a community, and community is what Instagram's algorithm consistently rewards.

How AI Examines Instagram's Algorithm

Instagram uses AI to personalize Feed, Stories, Reels, and the "Explore" page by predicting what each user is most likely to engage with. It evaluates signals like watch time, saves, shares, and relationship strength to decide what content to show and to whom.

Each surface has slightly different ranking priorities, but the goal is the same: keep users engaged longer.
Three core factors influence what people see most often:

• Interest — content similar to what users already engage with
  • Timeliness — newer posts generally get priority
  • Relationship — content from accounts users interact with frequently
Understanding these signals helps you create content that reaches your audience more effectively.

• A strong hook in the first 3 seconds
  • Trending or familiar audio
  • A concise length (often 7-30 seconds, depending on content type)
These elements help stop the scroll and keep viewers watching.

What Makes TikTok Unique

TikTok is built around the For You Page, where most views come from discovery, not followers. The platform shows videos based on what people watch, rewatch, and engage with, not who posted them. Instead of prioritizing who you are, TikTok prioritizes how your content performs. Even brand-new accounts can reach large audiences if their videos hold attention.

blocks.text:
Every TikTok video starts with a small test audience. If those viewers watch most or all of the video, interact with it, or share it, TikTok expands distribution — gradually pushing it to larger groups.

This performance-based testing is what fuels TikTok's viral effect. Follower count plays little role in that process.
What Makes TikTok Content Go Viral?
Virality isn't random; it follows repeatable patterns. When you understand them, you can create intentionally.
High-performing TikToks usually combine four elements:

• Trending sounds — TikTok favors familiar audio
  • Strong hooks — the first 1-2 seconds stop the scroll
  • Authentic delivery — real and relatable beats overproduced
  • Fast value — entertainment or insight delivered quickly (often under 60 seconds)
Using these patterns significantly improves your odds of going viral.

blocks.text: Authenticity Over Polish

So, why does authenticity matter so much on TikTok? Because it directly affects whether people keep watching, which is what the algorithm cares about most.

Unlike follower-driven platforms, TikTok prioritizes watch time and engagement. When your content feels relatable and personality-driven, viewers stay longer — and the longer they watch, the more TikTok pushes your content to new audiences.
Polish can help, but if it sacrifices authenticity, people scroll past. Authenticity keeps them hooked.
Creating Authentic TikTok Content With AI

Now that you understand why authenticity matters, the next question is practical: how do you consistently create authentic TikTok content — especially when managing content as an SMM? This is where AI becomes a support tool: it helps you plan what to say and how to structure it, while you deliver it in a real, human way.
How AI supports authenticity instead of killing it:

• Idea generation, not scripting every word: AI helps outline the message, not force robotic delivery.
  • Hook suggestions based on patterns: You choose what feels natural.
  • Clarity and pacing: AI trims fluff so the message lands faster.
  • Consistency across videos: Without repeating the same phrasing.

Working with Video Length

TikTok doesn't reward a single standard video length — it rewards the right length for the right type of content.

Short videos are easier to finish, while longer ones only work if they keep attention with a clear payoff — especially on TikTok, where videos can be up to 10 minutes long, choosing the wrong length can break watch time even if the idea is good.

Hashtags & Captions

People activelysearch for content such as "beginner workouts," "day-in-the-life posts," or "small-business tips." Your caption and hashtags help TikTok categorize your video and show it to the right audience. But how to distinguish good hashtags from bad? Let's find out better hashtags through AI.

Niche tags connect you with a targeted, engaged audience actively seeking your specific content, driving meaningful interaction. Trending/platform-favored tags signal relevance to the algorithm, increasing chances of landing on the For You Page (FYP) and riding current momentum. Using a strategic mix optimizes for both reach and relevant engagement.

blocks.text: There are two effective ways to use Groups strategically:

• Create your own Group around a shared problem, identity, or goal
  • Participate actively in existing Groups where your ideal customers already gather
Both approaches work, but only when you lead with value, not promotion.
How Groups Work
Facebook Groups are communities where people with shared interests connect and share knowledge. Here's how to use them:
Creating your own Group:

1. Go to Facebook → Click "Groups" → Create "New Group."
  2. Name it around a specific problem or identity (e.g., "Social Media Managers for Small Business").
  3. Set privacy (Public or Private) and add a clear description.
  4. Create group rules (what's allowed, what's not).
  5. Invite 20-30 people from your network to start.
  6. Post valuable content 2-3 times weekly to keep engagement high.
Joining existing Groups:

1. Search for groups using niche keywords (e.g., "coffee shop owners").
  2. Join 3-5 active groups with regular engagement.
  3. Read the rules before posting.
  4. Engage authentically — comment, answer questions, share insights.
  5. Build relationships for 1-2 weeks before mentioning your services.
Facebook Events for Action
Groups help you build relationships and trust over time — but sometimes you want people to take a clear next step. That's where Facebook's action-driven formats come in.

If you want to drive registrations, attendance, or participation, Facebook Events are quite powerful and often underutilized. They're ideal for local businesses, workshops, webinars, launches, and both in-person and online events.
How Events Work
Facebook Events help you promote gatherings, webinars, workshops, or launches with built-in visibility and social proof. Let's see how to use them:
Creating your own Event:

1. Go to Facebook → Click "Events" in the left menu → "Create New Event"
  2. Choose event type: In-person, Virtual
  3. Add event details: Name, date, time, location/link, and description
  4. Upload an eye-catching cover image
  5. Set privacy: Public (anyone can see), Private (invite-only), or Group (members of a group)
  6. Invite your network and relevant groups
  7. Post updates regularly to keep attendees engaged

When you create an Event, Facebook gives it increased visibility through notifications and feeds — extending reach beyond your usual audience.

Events also introduce urgency and social proof. Seeing others interested or attending lowers hesitation and increases participation.

Beyond organic community building, Facebook also offers one of the most powerful advertising platforms available. While Groups and Events help you build relationships, Facebook Ads allow you to reach highly targeted audiences at scale.

How Groups Work
Facebook Groups are communities where people with shared interests connect and share knowledge. Here's how to use them:
Creating your own Group:

1. Go to Facebook → Click "Groups" → Create "New Group."
  2. Name it around a specific problem or identity (e.g., "Social Media Managers for Small Business").
  3. Set privacy (Public or Private) and add a clear description.
  4. Create group rules (what's allowed, what's not).
  5. Invite 20-30 people from your network to start.
  6. Post valuable content 2-3 times weekly to keep engagement high.

Joining existing Groups:

1. Search for groups using niche keywords (e.g., "coffee shop owners").
  2. Join 3-5 active groups with regular engagement.
  3. Read the rules before posting.
  4. Engage authentically — comment, answer questions, share insights.
  5. Build relationships for 1-2 weeks before mentioning your services.
Facebook Events for Action

1. Go to Facebook → Click "Events" in the left menu → "Create New Event"
  2. Choose event type: In-person, Virtual
  3. Add event details: Name, date, time, location/link, and description
  4. Upload an eye-catching cover image
  5. Set privacy: Public (anyone can see), Private (invite-only), or Group (members of a group)
  6. Invite your network and relevant groups
  7. Post updates regularly to keep attendees engaged

Analytics with AI

Welcome to Unit 3! Now that you've tried AI across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube, it's time to move to the next level — analyzing your performance and making efficient further decisions.

In this lesson, you'll learn how to use AI to interpret performance data, spot meaningful patterns, and turn raw metrics into clear, actionable decisions for your social media strategy.
Why Metrics Need Interpretation

Raw metrics show you what happened. Engagement rates, reach, saves, comments — these are numbers that don't explain why one post performed better than another or what you should do differently next time.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! Raw numbers tell you what happened, but the real value is in spotting patterns. Maybe your how-to videos outperform vlogs, or videos posted in the morning get more saves.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Either recreating a successful video or ignoring patterns means you're missing the bigger picture. Engagement is driven by what resonates with your audience.

options.label: Focus only on the video with the highest engagement and recreate it exactly
Assume engagement is random and don't dive into analytics
Look for one pattern and start experimenting randomly
Look for patterns across all videos: common themes, formats, posting times, or hooks to understand what drives engagement

blocks.question: You're reviewing your TikTok analytics and notice that your last five videos have very different engagement rates. What's the most effective way to turn this data into actionable insights?

blocks.text: Organizing Data for Analysis

The real value comes from connecting numbers to patterns: which themes resonate, which formats drive action, and when your audience is most engaged. 

But when posts are scattered across screenshots or inconsistent spreadsheets, AI can't reliably surface those connections.

Start by organizing your content into clear categories: theme, format, platform, date, and engagement metrics, so AI can accurately identify what's working and reveal patterns that aren't immediately apparent.
AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT are excellent at categorizing by themes — but they need clean, structured data to work with. This is where Gemini in Google Sheets comes in. Let's try it!

blocks.prompt: Ask Gemini in Google Sheets to organize your posts by theme.
blocks.template: I have social media data with the following columns: Post Title, Date, Platform, Likes, Comments, Shares, Saves. Add [what to add] that categorizes each post by [category] based on the post title.

Building a Portfolio
As an SMM specialist, your portfolio should demonstrate measurable business impact.

blocks.text: Crafting Personalized Outreach

After you've searched for the right client, you can use the same technique as you did to generate messages and set different tones and themes. AI tools like Claude are excellent at writing personalized outreach messages — but outreach needs to become ongoing engagement, which requires staying visible and building relationships over time. This is where Extrovert comes in.
Meet Extrovert

Extrovert is an AI-powered LinkedIn engagement tool that acts as your full-time ghostwriter for comments. 

It helps you stay consistently engaged with top leads by commenting thoughtfully on their latest LinkedIn posts without spending hours writing daily responses. It's like a bridge between "I sent the outreach message" and "I'm building a real relationship with this prospect."
Let's see how you can track and manage all your interactions in one place with Extrovert.
Step 1: Connect Your LinkedIn Account

1. Sign up for Extrovert and connect your LinkedIn account securely.
  2. Grant permission for Extrovert to access your feed and enable comment suggestions.
  3. Once connected, your dashboard will start populating with posts from your target prospects and leads.
Your LinkedIn engagement is now centralized and ready to track.
Step 2: Use the Dashboard to Track Engagement

1. View Contacted Prospects: See a list of everyone you've engaged with, including comment history and post summaries.
  2. Monitor Comment Performance: Track which comments get replies or spark conversations, helping you refine your engagement strategy.
  3. Set Engagement Goals: Schedule daily or weekly engagement targets to stay consistent without overwhelming yourself.
  4. Filter by Priority: Focus on high-value prospects first so your time goes to the leads that matter most.
What Extrovert Does

• Keeps you visible: Consistently engages with prospects' posts so you stay top of mind without manual effort.
  • Generates thoughtful comments: AI crafts contextual responses that add value, not just generic "Great post!" replies.
  • Saves time: Summarizes long posts instantly so you can engage meaningfully in seconds, not minutes.
  • Builds relationships over time: Regular, meaningful engagement turns cold outreach into warm connections.
You get your personalized outreach from Claude, then use Extrovert to stay engaged and build trust over time, turning one-off messages into long-term relationships.
How to Use the Extrovert Dashboard
Extrovert's dashboard gives you two ways to engage: use pre-built buttons for instant actions or add your own custom instructions for personalized responses.
Pre-built buttons include:

• Elaborate — Make the AI comment more detailed
  • Make short— Condense the comment while keeping the meaning
  • Ask a question — Turn it into a conversation starter
  • Make a joke — Make it sound warmer and more relatable
And many more for you to respond to easily!
When you type your own request in the command box, like "make this more professional" or use pre-built buttons, Extrovert adapts instantly to match your voice and engagement goals. Let's test it!

blocks.text: Building Blocks of Client Management

A simple client management system has a simple formula: Clear Expectations + Regular Communication + Proof of Results. To achieve that, you need to know how to provide a smooth client onboarding process that yields clear outcomes and satisfied clients.
What is Client Onboarding

Client onboarding is the process of welcoming new clients and setting the foundation for a successful working relationship. It ensures both you and your client are aligned on expectations, timelines, and deliverables from the very start. A strong onboarding process prevents miscommunication, builds trust, and sets the tone for a long-term partnership.

feedbackCorrect.text: Poor onboarding creates confusion around scope, availability, and deliverables, leading to frustration on both sides. Clear expectations from day one = fewer surprises later.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Questions are normal and healthy in client relationships — they show engagement. The real problems come from unclear scope, missed expectations, and surprise complaints about what's "included." A strong onboarding process addresses all of these upfront, so both you and the client are aligned from the start.

Final Onboarding Step

The last piece of successful onboarding is defining how clients will approve your work. Without a clear approval process, you'll face confusion, delays, and last-minute changes that derail your schedule.
Set clear expectations upfront:

• Where approvals happen: Shared folder, project management tool, or email?
  • Approval deadline: How much time do clients have to review?
  • What happens if they don't respond: Will you proceed with scheduling, or pause until they approve?
  • Revision limits: How many rounds of edits are included?
A defined approval process protects your time, keeps projects on schedule, and ensures clients stay engaged without last-minute surprises.

The real problems come from unclear scope, missed expectations, and surprise complaints about what's "included." A strong onboarding process addresses all of these upfront, so both you and the client are aligned from the start.

Many social media managers lose clients not because of poor results, but because of confusion and mismatched expectations. A strong onboarding process sets the tone for a long-term relationship and helps you stand out as a professional. 

Let's create a reusable checklist that covers everything your clients need to know from day one.

blocks.prompt: Ask Notion AI to build a reusable onboarding checklist.

blocks.text:
Now that you have a reusable onboarding checklist, follow it to have a smooth onboarding process. 

First, let's try creating a communication guidelines email for future clients.

blocks.exampleResponse: Subject: How We'll Stay Connected Hello [Client Name], I'm excited to work with you! To keep our collaboration smooth, this is how we'll communicate: Response Times: I typically respond within 24 hours on weekdays. For urgent requests, I'll do my best to reply within a few hours. Best Way to Reach Me: Email is best for project updates and approvals. For quick questions, feel free to message me on [Slack/WhatsApp/preferred platform]. Availability: I'm available Monday-Friday, 9 AM-6 PM [your timezone]. I don't check messages on weekends, but I'll catch up first thing Monday morning. Urgent Requests: If something truly urgent comes up, text me at [phone number], and I'll prioritize it. Looking forward to a great partnership! Best, [Your Name]

blocks.template: Write a professional email to a new client explaining [communication type]. Include: response time expectations, preferred communication channels, availability hours, and how to [action]. Keep it friendly and under 150 words.

blocks.text: But communication guidelines are only the first step. Once a client knows what to expect, your next move determines whether they trust you or start worrying. What should you do next?

feedbackCorrect.text: Right! Proactive communication prevents anxiety and complaints. Clients who know what's happening trust you more and complain less.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Waiting for clients to ask or relying only on deliverables creates uncertainty. Regular communication, even when there's "nothing to report," builds trust and prevents problems.

options.label: Communicate regularly on progress and results, so they never have to wonder what's happening
Assume the client will reach out if anything matters and only respond when prompted
Focus purely on deliverables and let results speak for themselves
Send them everything at once so they have all the information

blocks.question: You've onboarded a client with clear guidelines and expectations. What's the most important thing to do next?

blocks.text: Regular Communication: The Trust Builder

During onboarding, we need to create communication schedules.

When clients don't hear from you, they may start to wonder if something was missed or if they're not a priority — even when everything is running smoothly.
The next logical step is to learn how to avoid losing contact with clients and keep them updated. Let's use Gemini to draft a weekly content preview email template you can customize and reuse!

blocks.exampleResponse: Subject: Weekly Content Preview: [Date Range] Hi [Client Name], I hope you’re having a great week! I’ve just finished drafting our content for the upcoming week. Here is a quick look at our posting schedule: Monday: [Topic/Post Type] Wednesday: [Topic/Post Type] Friday: [Topic/Post Type] How to provide feedback: Please review the drafts in [Link to Folder/Tool] and leave any comments or approvals by [Day/Time]. If I don't hear from you by then, I’ll move forward with scheduling to stay on track! Excited to get these live, [Your Name]

blocks.text: After creating a weekly communications schedule, let's take it a step further. Communication doesn't stop at previews; clients also need to see the results of your work. That's where monthly reports come in.
Monthly Reports: Proof of Value

Monthly reports serve one purpose: prove your work is worth paying for. 

Without reports, clients forget what you've done. But with reports, clients see what you delivered, what worked, and what's next. Now, let's ask ChatGPT to create a monthly report structure.

blocks.exampleResponse: Here's a clean, shortened monthly performance report template you can reuse for social media management. 1. Month in Review — Key metrics snapshot (engagement, reach, follower growth) — Overall performance summary (what changed vs. last month) — One-line takeaway: how the account performed overall 2. What Worked — Top-performing posts or formats — Content themes that resonated most — Quick insight on why these worked (timing, hook, format, topic) 3. Next Month's Plan — Content focus or themes to double down on — What we’ll test or adjust — Primary goals for the upcoming month

blocks.template:
Create a shortened monthly [document type] template for [service].

blocks.text: Once you have your monthly report template, you can:

• Use them to create reports for your clients, keeping them informed about progress, results, and upcoming strategy.
  • Save it to reuse and modify for future clients — just update the data and insights each month
This template becomes a time-saving asset that keeps communication consistent and professional across all your client relationships.
Final Onboarding Step

The last piece of successful onboarding is defining how clients will approve your work. Without a clear approval process, you'll face confusion, delays, and last-minute changes that derail your schedule.
Set clear expectations upfront:

• Where approvals happen: Shared folder, project management tool, or email?
  • Approval deadline: How much time do clients have to review?
  • What happens if they don't respond: Will you proceed with scheduling, or pause until they approve?
  • Revision limits: How many rounds of edits are included?
A defined approval process protects your time, keeps projects on schedule, and ensures clients stay engaged without last-minute surprises.

feedbackCorrect.text: Exactly! If your onboarding clearly stated "if I don't hear from you by [deadline], I'll proceed with scheduling," then you're following the agreed process. This keeps projects on track and teaches clients to respect deadlines.

feedbackIncorrect.text: Waiting indefinitely teaches clients that deadlines don't matter and puts you behind schedule. A clear approval process, agreed upon during onboarding, allows you to proceed professionally when deadlines pass, keeping projects moving forward.

Wait until they respond — better safe than sorry
Send multiple follow-up messages until they respond
Proceed with scheduling as outlined in your approval process and notify them

blocks.text: Scaling Beyond One Client
Now that you know how to follow the onboarding checklist and deliver client-friendly reports, it's time to learn how to manage multiple clients at once.

Managing every client manually can feel overwhelming — but here’s the good news: when your processes are simple and repeatable, scaling becomes much easier. Scaling means systemizing what you do, automating repetitive tasks, and using tools to manage workflows.
For the final step, let's use Notion AI to create a weekly workflow checklist for easier task tracking that works for any client.

With a weekly checklist, you can focus on strategy and creativity rather than manually tracking every small step.
